timing_register_audit.timestamp: Clock destination formed by LEA EDX,[ESP+18] at B33C6B and pushed before current clock slot20 call. FILD signed64 ticks at +18 and frequency at +20; FDIVP then FSTP float at +14.

timing_register_audit.delta: FCOMIP/POP then JBE takes nonpositive or unordered path. SSE subtracts delta from negative-zero D7A208 (0x80000000). This is not an absolute-value C++ substitute or a wrap-period correction.
timing_register_audit.rate: First read MOV ECX,[ESI+18] at B33CC2 and TEST determines sign branch; second current read FILD DWORD[ESI+18] at B33CD1. timing_register_audit.decision: FDIVP ST2,ST0 computes retained1000/rate; FCOMIP/POP and JBE reject below/equal/unordered. Source SETA matches the taken condition; rate0 is not replaced by an artificial success/default rate.
timing_register_audit.publication: Accepted native path reloads rounded sample at B33CE4 and publishes at B33CEA before loading callback1C and current context20. Source does the same. Fresh fixture reaches only the rejected-sample worker path.
timing_register_audit.boundary: The helper uses the same x87/SSE arithmetic and incoming modes, but the new C++ interface/compiler frame is not native private-frame/register/exception ABI identity. Fresh timing comparisons cover nearest and downward x87 rounding in the fixture environment, not every FP trap/MXCSR/async state.

failure_retention_and_stop_limits: Worker constructor has no local EH rollback. If the second event allocation throws, the first event and earlier field writes remain; the supplied raw owner is still caller-owned. Source allocation uses existing malloc/new-handler retry then bad_alloc behavior, not an invented successful null object.

CreateEvent may return a null handle inside a real event wrapper. CreateThread may return null; its result is stored and still passed to SetThreadPriority and ResumeThread. Their failure results are ignored as in native. No retries, replacement threads or fabricated event successes are added.

Destructor sets shutdown but does not clear run. It signals captured wake, attempts an infinite wait, then closes current handle. With a null/invalid handle, the wait/close results do not prove a successful join. With a valid handle, run staying nonzero can prevent exit indefinitely.

Shutdown is not tested inside the run loop, timing loop, callback or renderer-busy loop. A callback or substantive Begin/End provider that does not return, or a busy renderer that never clears, prevents the stop acknowledgement/join.

Existing B33BF0 stop helper clears run and waits on current idle event; it does not wake an initially sleeping worker. Callers must obey the real wake/run/idle protocol. The fixture starts and signals run before asking for stop, then waits for acknowledgement before scalar deletion.

If a context/profile contract error or provider C++ exception escapes the Win32 thread entry, no source catch, idle acknowledgement or normal ExitThread result is supplied. Such failures are outside the returning-worker domain; do not label them recoverable game errors.

Event/profile contexts must survive until all workers have actually joined. Failed construction with retained acquisitions does not justify releasing borrowed providers or rebinding the immutable process pointer.

Volatile accesses preserve intended current field reads, but arbitrary concurrent mutations and C++ data-race equivalence remain unproved. Native SEH/asynchronous faults and original thread-private stack identity are not validated.
